author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Writing under James I, Shakespeare brought questions of succession, loyalty and kingship before a court and public audience. Macbeth gives political ambition the intimacy of a married couple's conversation.

hook.text: What would you do if you were promised the life you secretly wanted?

paragraphs: Macbeth hears that he will become king. The words do not give him a plan. They give his imagination somewhere to go.

The frightening part is how quickly possibility becomes pressure. A future he had not openly claimed begins to feel like something he could lose. His wife understands the desires and doubts involved, and their conversations make a great public crime emerge from private persuasion.

Shakespeare follows what happens when a person tries to secure a life that can no longer feel secure. Every obstacle can begin to look like permission for another wrong. Sleep, ordinary company and the simple experience of being at home become difficult.
Read for the small verbal steps by which an imagined action becomes necessary. When has wanting something made you start treating the fact that you could have it as a reason why you should?

orientation.text: The play moves quickly through prophecy, persuasion and political consequence. Notice what the predictions actually say and what Macbeth adds to them.
